ledger.claim: The recorded distances settle the deviation: the platform records 17.6 km actually driven against a 16.2 km recommended route, a deviation of 1.40 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. The case therefore cannot fall in the within-tolerance rows of the refund matrix, and a refund row is live.

The route actually taken is not in dispute and the trace that shows it is clean: the driver-device trace carries 57 fixes at 30 s intervals, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s and a map-matched road on every fix, and it puts the vehicle on the Central Expressway to 10:48:41 and on Upper Thomson Road from 10:49:11, matching the recorded deviation at 10:49:23 and the rejoin at Balestier Road / Thomson Road at 11:03:14. POL-RD-22 makes the trace the record of which route was taken and when.

POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data intersects the recommended route, and the only advisory on file does not establish that intersection. The HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory is on the Central Expressway towards the City at 'after Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1 exit to PIE' and overlaps the trip window, but its own derived fields leave intersects_route and justifies_reroute null, and the derivation states in terms that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The intersection limb of POL-RD-23 is therefore not made out on this record.

The driver's own words are not traffic data. His chat message 'Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?' is a party's assertion, and POL-RD-23 provides that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The chat artifact EV-CHAT-06012 is impaired at weight 0.9 on issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, and I disclose that; it is cited here only for the text of that message, which is what the driver said, not for any fact the impairment touches.

Because the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation is over 1 km, row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the excess distance fare is refunded in full: the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD, which the fare breakdown computes as 1.01 SGD. The rider filed this dispute, so PARTIAL_REFUND returns that sum to the rider; the rider presses for the matrix's own measure of the excess, 1.01 SGD, and not the 4.80 SGD headline, because the matrix is the remedy the policy provides and the rider asks for nothing the policy does not give.

Rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 both refund the excess distance fare; the only row that leaves the rider carrying the whole charge is row (a), which needs a traffic-justified reroute that the rider was informed of and agreed to. The rider does not dispute the chat: the driver asked at 10:46:33 and the rider answered 'Ok can, thanks' at 10:47:03, before the point of deviation, which would satisfy POL-RD-21's agreement limb. But that acknowledgment is carried solely by EV-CHAT-06012, which is impaired at weight 0.9 on SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH, so POL-GEN-02(2) caps any finding that turns on it at 0.9, while the driver's profile carries fraud_flags of 2, which under POL-GEN-22 lifts the confidence required for an AI ruling to 0.95. A row (a) NO_ACTION that leaves the rider paying the excess cannot be entered at the confidence the policy demands, and the case must be resolved on a row that does not depend on the impaired chat.

If the Judge is not persuaded that the advisory fails the intersection limb, but is also unable to find from the record that it meets it, then the traffic-justification fact POL-RD-23 needs cannot be established on this evidence, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation with the open question stated rather than an outcome inferred from the gap. POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-03 carry ESCALATE for this category, and on an escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge.

The deviation is established as 1.40 km, and it is over the tolerance: POL-RD-22 measures deviation as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km, the platform's recorded distances, and this record carries 17.60 km actual against 16.20 km recommended. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, which puts the case in the 'over 1 km' limb of the POL-RD-24 matrix. The trip record is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance (POL-RD-22).

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider of a deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. The chat shows exactly that: the driver wrote at 10:46:33 'Hi, CTE jam until PIE, I go Upper Thomson then Thomson Road ok?' - a brief reason, which the clause says is enough - and the rider answered at 10:47:03 'Ok can, thanks'. DISCLOSURE under POL-GEN-02(1): the chat artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.9; the issue code that fired is SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH (severity LOW), a version tag on an export that is not truncated and whose four messages map one-to-one, and it does not touch the acknowledgement recorded.

ledger.claim: The 4.80 SGD the rider claims has no basis in the policy's arithmetic. POL-RD-24 fixes the only sum the matrix can return on this record at the excess distance fare - deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge - which is 1.40 x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD, and that only on rows (b) and (d), neither of which applies here. The ledger confirms per_km_rate_sgd 0.72, total_charged 21.41 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the claimed figure is overstated several times over on the rider's own best case.

The notice and the acknowledgement do not stand or fall on the impaired chat export. The COMPLETE trip record, weight 1.0, independently lists MSG-06012-003 (driver, 10:46:33) and MSG-06012-004 (rider, 10:47:03) in its messages_during_trip block, and POL-GEN-02(2) takes the highest weight among independent artifacts carrying the deciding fact. The single impairment in this record - the chat log at 0.9 for SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH - therefore does not lower the weight of the agreed-deviation finding, and I name it rather than presenting it as clean.

This is a case the AI may finish on this record. The contested amount is 4.80 SGD, and the facts that decide it - the recorded distances, the message timestamps, the advisory window and its type - all rest on COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0, the only impairment being a 0.9 schema tag on the chat export. Whatever elevated confidence POL-GEN-22 requires where a profile carries fraud flags is met on this record, and POL-RD-25's condition on an AI ruling is satisfied, so no escalation is called for.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider (R-15817) and the driver (D-43200):

WHAT IS SETTLED. The deviation is not in doubt. The trip record EV-TRIP-06012 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records 17.6 km actually driven against a 16.2 km recommended route — 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22 — and the GPS trace EV-GPS-06012 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) confirms which route was taken and when. This is an over-tolerance case, so the within-tolerance rows of the POL-RD-24 matrix are out.

WHY THE AI CANNOT FINISH IT. Two matters then decide the case, and neither can be carried to the confidence this dispute requires (POL-GEN-22 sets 0.95 because the driver's profile carries fraud_flags 2; POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-23's sibling rules send an under-confidence route-deviation case to a human).

(1) Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The only traffic data on file is the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-06012-01 — HEAVY_TRAFFIC (an admissible congestion class), on the Central Expressway towards the City, window 10:16–11:26, which covers the trip. The CTE is a leg of the recommended route (Canberra Link → SLE → CTE → Balestier Road) and the advisory is in the direction of travel, so on the better view it intersects the recommended route and the reroute is traffic-justified; I do not accept that it is affirmatively non-justified, and I therefore do not enter row (d). But the advisory's own derived record leaves 'intersects the recommended route' undetermined and states the record does not say whether it lies on the recommended route, so if that fact is treated as not established, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human on that open question. Either way the traffic limb is not something an AI ruling can close at 0.95.

(2) Informing and agreement (POL-RD-21; POL-RD-24 row (a)). If the reroute is traffic-justified, the only row that leaves the rider carrying the fare is row (a) — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, over 1 km, no refund. Row (b) is unavailable because the rider was informed. The informing and the agreement rest on the chat log EV-CHAT-06012, which is IMPAIRED: weight 0.9, issue SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence on any finding that turns on it is capped at 0.9, below the 0.95 POL-GEN-22 requires, so a row (a) NO_ACTION cannot be entered. The driver's argument that EV-TRIP-06012 independently carries the messages does not lift the cap: that block lists only the message ids, senders and timestamps (MSG-06012-003 at 10:46:33, MSG-06012-004 at 10:47:03), not their text, so the content of the informing and the agreement is carried by the 0.9 chat alone.

THE ARITHMETIC. The rider's 4.80 SGD headline has no basis in POL-RD-24 in any event. The excess distance fare the matrix can return is the deviation distance times the per-km rate: 1.40 × 0.72 = 1.01 SGD (EV-FARE-06012). That figure would be the refund only on row (b) or row (d), and I do not find row (d) made out; so no refund issues.

OUTCOME. The case is escalated. Both amounts are null and the 4.80 SGD in dispute is held, not collected or refunded. Open question for the human reviewer: whether the LTA advisory intersects the recommended route, and if it does, whether the rider's acknowledgment (chat log, weight 0.9, SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH) can be relied on at the 0.95 confidence the driver's fraud flags require.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
